outcome: maternal outcomes (urine albumin, abruption with PPH, DIC, eclampsia, PPH, severe preeclampsia)
mode of birth (elective LSCS, NVD, emergency LSCS, forceps assisted vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included pregnant women aged 18-35 years with singleton pregnancies and at least 20 weeks gestation, all diagnosed with pregnancy-induced hypertension.
finding: Higher serum LDH levels were associated with an increased risk of severe preeclampsia and were indicative of overall maternal and fetal complications.
mod_finding: No statistically significant association was found between different serum LDH levels and the mode of birth (NVD, elective LSCS, emergency LSCS, or forceps assisted vaginal delivery).
